penalties_description: Violations subject to enforcement under China's Tax Collection and Administration Law. The new VAT Law outlines penalties for non-compliance; specific penalty quantum deferred to the Tax Administration Law.
verbatim_quote: Under the DPI framework, a digital platform that facilitates transactions between sellers and customers may be required to act as the VAT intermediary for supplies made through the platform.
notes: China's consolidated VAT Law (passed 25 December 2024) and its Implementation Regulations both took effect 1 January 2026, replacing the Interim VAT Regulations. The Digital Platform Intermediary (DPI) framework places VAT reporting and, in some cases, payment obligations on platforms facilitating transactions; full deemed-supplier rules are still evolving and Detailed Implementation Regulations are awaited. The general-taxpayer registration threshold is CNY 5 million annual taxable sales; small-scale taxpayers below CNY 5 million use a simplified 3% levy rate (temporarily reduced to 1% through 31 December 2027). Standard rate of 13% applies to most goods; 9% and 6% apply to specified services. Import VAT collected by customs at point of entry. No explicit USD registration threshold is published; the CNY 5 million figure (~USD 690,000 at approximate exchange) is the statutory threshold. Overseas businesses face administrative barriers to VAT registration as no formal non-resident registration procedure has yet been established. Marketplace/platform obligations for foreign-established operators remain nascent and continue to evolve. USD equivalent of CNY 5 million threshold is an approximation and is not stated in source.
